key_insight: Greater night-to-night sleep variability was associated with prolonged post-enrollment hospitalization in acute psychiatric inpatients.
clinical_relevance: Sleep variability from wearable actigraphy or routine nursing observations may offer a practical marker for studying prolonged inpatient stays.
method: Prospective observational study of 94 acute psychiatric inpatients.
Sleep variability measured as each patient's standard deviation of nightly total sleep time across 5–7 available observations.
Age- and sex-adjusted logistic regression assessed post-enrollment stays exceeding 24 days.
evidence_signal: There were 23 prolonged-stay events; actigraphy-derived variability had an adjusted OR of 2.30 per additional hour (95% CI 1.08–4.93), with model AUC 0.756 versus 0.692 for age and sex alone.
watch_item: This small observational cohort establishes association, not causation or clinical readiness; observations were often nonconsecutive and began after enrollment rather than admission.
paper_title: Sleep Variability From Routine Nursing Observation and Wearable Actigraphy and Post-Enrollment Length of Stay in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients: Prospective Observational Study
